messages:
Maya Chen: Quick sync — we need to recalibrate RICE for the upcoming quarter around Sequencing vs Batching. Customer asks (multi-tenant batching) are loud and the infra team flagged latency risk.
Jules Park: Agree. Do we have concrete impact estimates for the top two customer asks? My gut says batching helps cost but hurts p95 latency.
Samir Patel: From usage signals: top 3 customers would reduce token cost by ~18% with batching. Activation uplift estimate is small (2-3%) because UX latency may drop conversions.
Ana Ortiz: Larger enterprise asks include SLA parity and predictable tail latency; they might churn if p95 degrades. That's high impact.
Leo Zhang: Engineering effort: batching core is medium (3-4 sprints) because we need cross-model KV cache changes + rollout infra. Sequencing (launch order controls) is low effort (1 sprint) and can unblock some experiments.
Maya Chen: So looks like Impact: batching = medium-high (cost savings + enterprise), sequencing = medium (enables experiments). Effort: batching = high, sequencing = low. Risk: batching = high (tail latency), sequencing = low.
Jules Park: RICE inputs — can someone assign numbers? I'll propose Reach: batching = 40% of active orgs, sequencing = 60% (affects internal launches). Impact (0-10): batching = 6, sequencing = 4. Confidence: batching = 0.6, sequencing = 0.7. Effort (months): batching = 3, sequencing = 0.5.
Samir Patel: Quick calc: RICE score approx. batching = (40*6*0.6)/3 = 48; sequencing = (60*4*0.7)/0.5 = 336. Big delta.
Ana Ortiz: That's a huge swing — sequencing looks like a clear win by RICE, but it doesn't capture long-term cost savings for top customers.
Leo Zhang: We should consider sequencing as a short-term win to enable guardrails and telemetry, then batch incrementally for the largest customers after validating.
Maya Chen: Proposal: 1) Prioritize sequencing this quarter to unlock experiments and reduce release risk. 2) Do a focused P0 spike for batching (1 sprint) to de-risk latency and quantify p95 impact. 3) If spike looks good, schedule batching as a Dedicated-only feature next quarter (so hosted unaffected).
Jules Park: +1. Also add launch criteria for batching: p95 increase < 10% on Dedicated configs OR can be mitigated with adaptive routing fallback.
Samir Patel: For the spike, I'll own instrumentation: perf suite across sequence lengths, model families, and a "worst-case" KV cache flush test.
Ana Ortiz: I'll bring customer success into the loop — get explicit commitments from two pilot customers for Dedicated batching pilot.
Leo Zhang: I'll scope the sequencing work and break into canary flags + rollout plan, estimate 2 engineers for 4 weeks.
release-bot: Deploy scheduled: 'canary/sequence-feature' created. Runbook link: https://internal.runbook/release-sequence
Maya Chen: Great. Action items: Jules — update RICE doc with these numbers and the proposed plan; Samir — perf spike plan; Ana — customer pilot outreach; Leo — sequencing tickets + rollout plan. Check-in Friday.
Jules Park: Will do, adding a note to the roadmap board and tagging stakeholders. :thumbsup:
Ana Ortiz: Adding CS owners now.
Samir Patel: Spike tests scheduled for Wed.
Leo Zhang: Tickets in Jira: PROD-8421, PROD-8422. Assigning to eng-squad.
Maya Chen: Thanks all — aim to keep batch as a measurable outcome, not a checkbox. Friday sync to confirm next steps.
